mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign Notary Public in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization through Egyptian Embassy or Consulate (Egypt is not a Hague Apostille contracting state)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Certificate of Incorporation / Good Standing of Corporate Parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry of the foreign parent's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization through Egyptian Embassy or Consulate preceded by local Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate Secretary / Board of Directors of the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Consular Legalization at the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Passport Copies and Proof of Address of UBOs and Managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the jurisdiction of each UBO or manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization through the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate, with local MFA legalization where applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all officers, managers, shareholders, and UBOs against the Central Bank of Egypt sanctions list, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, and Politically Exposed Persons databases. Screening must be completed prior to filing, renewed during any shareholding change, and documented for retention by the AML compliance officer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Company Establishment Automation Portal; Commercial Registry names clearance module at the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company must have an operative Arabic name; a transliterated or supplementary foreign name may be filed for banking and contract purposes. All Arabic-language naming must conform to commercial naming conventions and must not conflict with existing registered names. English transliteration is accepted for the commercial registry if submitted together with the Arabic name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying state sponsorship without prior ministerial approval
Names already lawfully registered by any existing entity in the same sector
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, GAFI issues a written reasoned refusal with the grounds and legal basis. The applicant may file an administrative appeal with the GAFI Name Clearance Committee within 30 days of the refusal, submitting evidence of distinctiveness, prior use, or any required ministerial waiver. If the committee confirms refusal, the applicant may petition the competent Administrative Court in Cairo within 60 days from the final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted acceptance. GAFI and the Egyptian tax authority may accept a registered agent address for official correspondence and service of process, but the Commercial Registry requires the company to file a duly notarized lease or sublease agreement demonstrating legal occupation of a physical office in Egypt. Virtual offices without any physical footprint are generally not accepted for statutory incorporation and tax card issuance, particularly for advertising and media-buying companies generating income in Egypt.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate annual risk of approximately 20-30%. GAFI, Ministry of Investment, and tax inspection officers conduct unannounced physical visits to verify the existence of the registered office, personnel, and operative activities, especially for newly incorporated service entities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for LLC formation services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official government filing fee and tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation notice in the Official Gazette (Egyptian Egyptian Fact for Companies)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egypt Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009 and Law No. 94 of 2015; Articles 1–29 (formation and incorporation), Article 32 (board resolutions), Article 40 (registration with the Commercial Registry).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department, One-Shop System, Cairo
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (Aqd al-Ta'sis wa al-Nizam al-Dakhili) submitted through the GAFI e-registration portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an LLC under Law No. 159/1981; the capital must be fully subscribed and adequate to support the company's operations. Paid-up capital must be deposited in a temporary Egyptian bank account and a bank certificate submitted to GAFI; no escrow account is required except for in-kind capital contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned subscribers, having agreed to form a Limited Liability Company under the name [Company Name] LLC, do hereby subscribe to the total issued shares as set forth in the Articles of Association and irrevocably undertake to pay the paid-up portion in proportion to their respective holdings. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at the address stated in the preamble, and the Governor of [branch] is authorized to execute lease documents. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed General Manager and [Name] is appointed Finance Officer, each with the authority specified in the internal bylaws. All filings with GAFI are approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Trade Name Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI – Commercial Names Department (online via GAFI e-services portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed trade names in Arabic and English through the GAFI e-services platform; pay the name reservation fee; obtain a name reservation certificate valid for 60 days.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (if any)
Passport or national ID of each shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, file an administrative objection within 15 days or immediately submit alternate names for re-screening.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legalization and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Notary Office, Ministry of Justice, or certified notary public registered in Egypt
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOA and AOA in Arabic; have all shareholders or their legal representatives sign before a notary; the notary certifies signatures and affixes official stamps; then present the notarized documents to the GAFI revenue stamp unit for legal tax stamping.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney from non-resident shareholders (if formation is done through an agent)
Draft MOA and AOA in Arabic
Valid national ID or passport of every subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any deficiency identified by the notary and re-appear for a fresh notarization session; if translation is required, obtain an accredited certified translation and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Paid-up Capital Bank Deposit and Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any commercial bank operating under the Central Bank of Egypt
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account in the proposed LLC name; deposit the subscribed paid-up capital; obtain a bank deposit certificate stating the deposit amount, currency, account number, and date.
required_dossiers: Company name reservation certificate
Shareholders' valid identification documents
Notarized draft MOA and AOA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires final notarized MOA, coordinate with the notary to issue a certified copy; if the bank declines to open the account, request the name reservation certificate and approach another licensed bank within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – One-Stop Shop, Cairo, or GAFI branch offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assemble the full incorporation file pursuant to Law No. 159/1981 and submit it through the GAFI One-Stop Shop or e-portal. Verify identity of subscribers, pay the prescribed registration and publication fees, and obtain the certificate of incorporation and initial commercial registration extract.
required_dossiers: Notarized MOA and AOA
Bank capital deposit certificate
Company name reservation certificate
Lease agreement or registered office address declaration
First board resolution
National ID or passports of managers and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query, respond with supplementary documents within 10 working days; if the application is rejected, file an appeal with the GAFI Complaints Committee within 30 days of the rejection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Taxpayer Registration Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the incorporation certificate, register the LLC for income tax, value added tax, and payroll tax. File the unified tax registration form online or through the GAFI One-Stop Shop; obtain the tax card and VAT registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation issued by GAFI
Commercial registry extract
Lease contract or ownership deed of the registered office
Copy of shareholders' and managers' national IDs or passports
Board resolution authorizing the tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA requests additional proof of address or bank details, supply the requested documents within the legal deadline; if the application is rejected, re-submit after rectifying the indicated deficiencies through the ETA's support portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade – Commercial Registry Office, Cairo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the LLC is listed in the commercial register through the GAFI integration or file separately with the Commercial Registry. Upon listing, publish a summary of the incorporation in the company registry bulletin and pay the official gazette fees.
required_dossiers: GAFI registration certificate
Tax card and VAT certificate
Lease contract or registered office proof
Notarized board resolution
National ID or passport of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commercial registration details are rejected, amend the incorrect entries and re-file; if publication is delayed, request expedited processing with the registry department and obtain a stamped acknowledgment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial establishment license is required under Industrial Licensing Law No. 15 of 2017 for affiliate media buying and digital advertising services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No separate operating license is mandatory; the GAFI incorporation certificate and commercial registration serve as the operational authorization.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) – not applicable for non-industrial digital service operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based activity with no industrial discharge or emission
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, air emissions, or VOC thresholds apply; the company must comply with general provisions of Environmental Law No. 4 of 1994 (as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009) regarding office waste segregation, e-waste disposal through licensed recyclers, and energy efficiency.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The office premises must obtain a fire safety certificate from the General Administration of Civil Defense (Hay'at al-Difa' al-Madani) and a workplace safety clearance from the Ministry of Manpower and Migration. These clearances are required before commencing occupancy and must be renewed annually; inspections cover fire extinguishers, emergency exits, electrical load, and structural safety for the leased office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) at the Ministry of Finance, administered through the official ETA e-services portal and the National Single Window for Foreign Trade (NAFEZA); the E-Invoice and E-Receipt platform is operated by ETA for digital fiscal clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC (EG_LLC) obtains a unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) by completing ETA registration via the e-services portal or at the competent Tax Office. Steps: (1) obtain Commercial Registration certificate from the Egyptian Commercial Registry and any required establishment license; (2) file the ETA registration application with the LLC incorporation deed, board resolution, power of attorney, certificate of residence for foreign shareholders, proof of registered office address or lease, bank account details, and any home-state TIN; (3) apply simultaneously for VAT registration if the estimated taxable turnover exceeds the statutory threshold; (4) undergo ETA validation and receive the unified TIN certificate and, if applicable, the VAT registration certificate; (5) enrol in the e-invoice and e-receipt system and obtain the API integration credentials before issuing taxable invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: an Egyptian LLC is a resident juridical person taxed at entity level on its worldwide income, including revenue, capital gains, and interest under Income Tax Law No. 91/2005; the LLC is not treated as a pass-through entity. It is also a VAT person when taxable supplies exceed the registration threshold; the standard territorial scope is national Egypt-wide with no sub-national income tax distinction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not provide US-style check-the-box elections or hybrid-mismatch flow-through elections for an LLC; an Egyptian LLC is per se a taxable corporation. Available statutory elections include: (i) consolidated tax filing for resident corporations meeting the ownership and control conditions under the Income Tax Law; (ii) voluntary VAT registration below the mandatory threshold; (iii) simplified SME or small-taxpayer VAT computation where eligible; (iv) investment and Special Economic Zone incentives under Investment Law No. 72/2017 and the Suez Canal Economic Zone framework; (v) arm's-length transfer-pricing documentation and depreciation method choices permitted by the ETA. No hybrid mismatch election is recognised; substance and the arm's-length principle govern all transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) under Egyptian Law No. 67/2016, as amended, together with selective excise and stamp duty legislation
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies of goods and EGP 1,000,000 of annual taxable supplies of services for mandatory VAT registration, with voluntary registration available below the threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt mandates E-Invoice and E-Receipt digital fiscal clearance. Every VAT-registered taxpayer must integrate an approved ERP or invoicing system with the ETA via REST API and transmit each tax invoice to the ETA platform immediately upon issuance. The ETA validates the invoice and returns a unique invoice code and QR code that constitute the fiscal digital stamp. No paper-only or non-stamped invoice is accepted for input VAT deduction or export zero-rating. B2C receipts are similarly transmitted under the E-Receipt regime. Taxpayers must obtain API credentials and complete technical integration before issuing any commercial invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated when physically exported from Egypt to a destination outside Egypt under customs supervision and evidenced by customs export documentation. Services are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident recipient for use and consumption outside Egypt, including advertising and media-buying services performed in Egypt but delivered to foreign advertisers for offshore audiences. The exporter must hold a valid VAT registration and export/import card, issue a compliant E-Invoice stating the 0% rate, maintain a signed export contract or service agreement, obtain transport and customs proof, and settle the sale through an Egyptian bank in foreign currency. If the service is supplied to, or consumed in, Egypt, the standard 14% VAT applies and reverse-charge rules may apply to imported digital advertising services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration issued through the Egyptian Customs Authority / NAFEZA single window
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or other recognised transport document evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by an Egyptian bank evidencing the receipt and credit of export proceeds in foreign exchange
Commercial invoice and export sale contract or purchase order
VAT E-Invoice with ETA-issued QR code and 0% rate
Certificate of origin or customs clearance certificate where required by the destination customs regime
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA and the Central Bank of Egypt cross-check customs export records, shipping manifests, E-Invoice data, and bank foreign-exchange ledgers. The 0% VAT rate is provisional until the export and the inward remittance are fully substantiated. Failure to obtain or maintain the prescribed documentation, or failure to repatriate export proceeds in foreign currency within the statutory period, results in withdrawal of the zero-rating, retrospective assessment of 14% VAT on the export value, delay interest, and administrative penalties. Fraudulent zero-rating claims, falsified customs or banking documents, or collusive invoicing expose the taxpayer to tax evasion proceedings under Law No. 67/2016, including VAT clawback, penal fines, prohibition from the E-Invoice and export facilitation systems, and imprisonment for responsible officers in wilful cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), acting under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law), together with the Foreign Exchange Committee and the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU). The CBE exercises exclusive authority over licensing of banks, foreign-exchange operations, capital-flow monitoring, and clearing system supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a unified free-floating exchange-rate regime as consolidated on 6 March 2024. Current-account convertibility is broadly available for bona fide trade, service, and digital-advertising disbursements once documentary evidence (contracts, tax invoices, statement of purpose) is presented to an authorized bank. Capital-account convertibility remains conditional: inbound foreign capital injections, profit repatriations, dividend remittances, and inter-company loan reparations are permitted but subject to CBE declaration/reporting, proof of foreign-fund registration, tax clearance, and the entity's good-standing in the Commercial Registry and Tax Authority databases. The practical hurdles are documentary completeness, beneficial-ownership disclosure, and the historical reliance on CBE registration of the original inbound capital to guarantee the future right of outward remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE instructions applicable to service exporters and revenue-generating digital-media/affiliate operations, the full value of export proceeds must be repatriated into Egypt exclusively through an authorized CBE-licensed bank within the contractual payment deadline, and in any event no later than 120 days from the date of the underlying export invoice or service-completion date, unless the bank has approved a documented deferral. The proceeds must be credited to the exporter's Egyptian bank account; historically, CBE circulars imposed mandatory conversion ratios ranging from 15% to 50% during the 2022-2023 FX rationing period. Following the 6 March 2024 float, the blanket mandatory conversion/surrender ratio is no longer codified; instead, exporters retain the proceeds in foreign currency or convert them to Egyptian pounds pursuant to a written agreement with their bank, with 100% of proceeds nonetheless required to flow through the authorized banking channel.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Multi-Currency Operational Account + Capital Escrow Sub-Account
Corporate Multi-Currency Operational Account + Capital Escrow Sub-Account
Corporate Multi-Currency Operational Account with Trade and FX Facilities
Corporate Operating and Trade Settlement Account
Corporate Operating Account with Cross-Border Clearing Capabilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Moderate, solely as auxiliary disbursement rails. Egyptian law does not currently license foreign electronic-money institutions (EMIs) or offshore digital banks (Wise, Mercury, Payoneer) to hold statutory corporate balances or to receive export/inbound capital for an Egyptian LLC. The CBE mandates that all export proceeds and foreign-capital inflows be credited through a CBE-licensed bank. Offshore EMIs may only be used for ancillary outbound payouts to affiliate partners or adventory platforms if the Egyptian bank is informed, the flows appear in the reconciled ledger, and the EMI counterparty satisfies the bank's AML/CFT assessment; they cannot replace the local primary banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical presence in principle. Under CBE AML/CFT instructions implementing Law No. 80 of 2002, the Egyptian bank must conduct an in-person corporate onboarding interview with the company's legal representative, at least one director, and the ultimate beneficial owner(s) before the account becomes operative. Remote or video-only onboarding is not generally permitted for non-resident shareholders or entities with digital-business profiles; notarized and apostilled/legalized corporate documents, certified passports, and executed UBO declarations must be delivered to the branch, with the meeting recorded on bank minutes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border disbursements to foreign ad-tech platforms and affiliate networks with irregular invoicing cycles, typical of performance media buying.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a complete corporate-compliance binder containing: Commercial Registry extract, valid tax card, VAT/e-invoicing registration evidence, UBO declaration, board resolution appointing authorized signatories, executed platform agreements with Google Ads/Meta/TikTok, monthly platform payout and reconciliation statements, pro-forma and final tax invoices issued by the Egyptian LLC, a 12-month cash-flow projection segmenting media-buy spend from arbitrage revenue, and the entity's AML manual including affiliate KYC, sanctions screening, and suspicious-transaction reporting policies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments routed to MENA-region ad networks or jurisdictions perceived as high-risk/low-tax, triggering enhanced counterparty due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare per-counterparty due-diligence files including official commercial-register evidence, licensing proof, sanctions and negative-news screening outputs, IP/domain-level verification, and a value-chain narrative explaining the advertiser-to-affiliate relationship with live attribution/traffic-log evidence (CPM/CPC/CPA contracts, performance dashboards, invoice alignment) demonstrating that the transactions represent bona fide digital media services rather than transfer-avoidance or third-party settlement orchestration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign non-resident ultimate beneficial owners combined with a newly formed LLC and no prior tax/account filing history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the foreign shareholder's bank-issued confirmation of account relationship and source of funds, audited shareholder-level financial statements, the Egyptian LLC's tax registration certificates, VAT filings (or proof of registration within deadline), articles of association demonstrating substance and management in Egypt, and a written capital-source memorandum tracing each inbound transfer, together with physical attendance by the UBO at the KYC interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of crypto, prepaid cards, or unregulated PSP accounts in the affiliate settlement flow representing an AML/CFT evasion risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Adopt and present the entity's treasury and settlement policy resolution prohibiting cryptocurrency settlement, cash-equivalent instruments, and unregulated payment intermediaries; attach the policy to the bank file along with template compliance clauses for every affiliate agreement, and provide a reconciliation statement proving all revenues are receivable only through regulated banking channels or licensed payment service providers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: the foreign shareholder executes a SWIFT MT103 transfer in USD or EUR to the Egyptian LLC's account at the designated CBE-licensed bank, using the payment purpose code 'Foreign Direct Investment under Law No. 72 of 2017' or 'Capital Increase / Share Subscription', accompanied by the shareholders' resolution, updated Articles of Association, tax-clearance certificates, and a CBE registration form completed by the bank. The inbound capital must be logged with the CBE to confer registered status and preserve the legal right of future profit and capital repatriation. Wire verification includes the bank's cross-check against the Commercial Registry name, UBO data, and an incoming-funds confirmation letter issued to the corporate client. No crypto transfer, third-party ACH pass-through, or split-wire method is permissible.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The permitted settlement matrix comprises: (1) SWIFT MT103 for high-value disbursements to ad platforms, affiliate partners, and media buying agencies where a complete audit trail is required; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) for larger infrastructural procurement with technology or tele-media vendors where title documents are exchanged; (3) corporate card and direct-debit rails for daily auction-based ad-spend settlement with Google Ads, Meta, TikTok, and other demand-side platforms, reconciled through the bank's acquiring network; and (4) local-currency clearing via CBE RTGS and ACH for balances converted at the unified exchange rate when paying domestic suppliers or receiving local-origin fees.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright USD/EGP currency forward contracts executed with the primary CBE-licensed bank for underlying commercial/revenue transactions
USD/EGP currency swaps for dual-currency working capital and staggered campaign-settlement exposure
Roll-over FX forward structures aligned with monthly media-buying and affiliate payout cycles

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) permitted only through an offshore banking counterpart and supported by documented trade-flow exposure, as the Egyptian banking channel does not freely open NDF positions without an underlying qualifying transaction
Spot FX conversion at the CBE unified daily reference rate for profit repatriation and service disbursements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal and Updated Corporate Data Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office under the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary of the initial commercial registration; renewal application must be filed no earlier than 30 calendar days before the renewal date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs an administrative fine of EGP 500 per month (approximately USD 16); continued non-renewal for more than 90 days triggers suspension of the commercial registration and potential administrative strike-off of the LLC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return with Audited Annual Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April of the year following the tax year ended 31 December; a tax extension may be granted only by reasoned ETA approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties accrue at 2% per month on the unpaid tax liability; underdeclaration penalties apply up to 40% of additional tax, and tax evasion penalties up to 200% of the tax due; extended non-compliance triggers enforced collection and judicial seizure of assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements Deposit with the Commercial Registry after Shareholders' Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days from the date of the annual general meeting approving the financial statements, and by no later than 30 June following the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the audited accounts may result in refusal of commercial registry renewal, administrative fines, and suspension of the company's certificate of good standing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian LLCs are required to appoint a registered certified auditor for the annual statutory audit under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, regardless of size or revenue; there is no statutory small-company audit exemption. The audited financial statements must be approved by the shareholders' annual general assembly.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), issued by the Ministry of Investment and International Cooperation, substantively convergent with IFRS; listed entities follow additional Cairo Stock Exchange requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For every shareholding transfer or UBO change, the LLC must update its internal UBO register within 15 days and notify the Commercial Registry with the amended shareholder statement; no separate annual UBO form is prescribed, but the annual commercial registry renewal declaration requires confirmation of current shareholders and beneficial owners. The manager must certify accuracy under penalty of false declaration.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 900 per year for registered office address and corporate agent services in Cairo or Alexandria
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,000 - USD 2,500 per year for statutory audit and preparation of audited financial statements.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday or preferential CIT rate applies to an ordinary Egyptian onshore LLC engaged in ISIC 7310 affiliate media buying. The main effective-rate lever is the deduction of direct performance-media costs: ad inventory, publisher traffic purchases, platform commissions, affiliate payouts, software subscriptions, and employee costs, provided they are arm's length, documented, and supported by invoices and bank trails. Free-zone or Special Economic Zone benefits are not assumed in this fact pattern.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) Corporate Income Tax Return - Form 20, filed electronically through the ETA E-Tax portal (tax.gov.eg).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly provisional income tax declarations and advance payments may be required for large-category taxpayers, with the annual Form 20 reconciling all provisional payments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the close of the fiscal year. For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return and full CIT settlement are due by 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: Commercial Registration No., Tax Card No., and ETA E-Tax account ID.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the ETA-issued Tax Identification Number (TIN) obtained at non-resident taxpayer registration. A foreign Commercial Registration number is not accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period and fiscal year-end date (DD/MM/YYYY).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the Egyptian LLC's fiscal year-end as approved in the ETA pre-registration; if the LLC follows a foreign parent fiscal calendar, the same period must be consistently reported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue / sales proceeds: all media-buying commissions, performance fees, affiliate payouts retained, platform rebates, and ad arbitrage revenue in EGP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize revenue in EGP based on invoices issued by the Egyptian LLC. Non-resident shareholders must not net foreign platform deductions inside this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs and expenses: ad spend, traffic acquisition, publisher settlement costs, SaaS/ad-server fees, sub-affiliate commissions, rent, salaries, depreciation, and other business operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All deductible costs must be incurred through the Egyptian LLC and documented in Egypt. Cross-border payments to related foreign media vendors must satisfy the arm's length standard.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss offset: gross revenue minus deductible expenses, then adjusted for disallowed expenses and tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners must ensure intercompany charges and owner compensation are included or removed per ETA transfer-pricing adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses offset: amount of accumulated tax losses claimed in the current year, capped at the five-year carryforward limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses realized by the same Egyptian LLC may be offset. Foreign affiliate losses and foreign branch losses are not deductible for Egyptian CIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computation: 22.5% applied to taxable income after loss offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The full 22.5% statutory rate applies unless a specific free-zone regime or treaty-based permanent establishment exemption is validly claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: Egyptian withholding tax credits on revenue, foreign tax credits under an applicable DTA, and any previously paid provisional CIT instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the foreign tax authority's Certificate of Residence and a beneficial ownership declaration when claiming treaty credits or reduced WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable after credits and instalments: final amount remitted to the ETA with Form 20.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The remitting account must be the Egyptian LLC's EGP bank account; payments cannot be made from a foreign shareholder account.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 20 triggers a fixed administrative late-filing fine under Law No. 91/2005, typically in the range of EGP 1,000 to EGP 10,000, plus a monthly delay surcharge of 2% on unpaid CIT for each month or part-month, capped at 20%. Unpaid CIT accrues statutory delay interest calculated on a daily basis by the ETA until settlement. Repeated non-filing can lead to suspension of tax clearance, enforced collection, asset attachment, and referral to criminal tax evasion procedures.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder wishing to apply the reduced dividend rate under an Egypt DTA must deliver to the Egyptian LLC a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's home tax authority, accompanied by a completed beneficial ownership declaration and the shareholding/ownership chain. The LLC submits a DTA relief request and supporting documents to the ETA International Taxation Department before making the dividend distribution; ETA pre-approval is the recommended protocol. If the 10% WHT is applied and a treaty lower rate is available, the non-resident must file an administrative refund/relief claim with the ETA within the applicable statutory limitation period, attaching the TRC, DTA article, and proof that the Egyptian LLC withheld and remitted the tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT is 20% for royalties, technical fees, software/service rights, and similar cross-border IP payments made by an Egyptian LLC, and 20% for interest paid to non-resident lenders. Under an applicable DTA, the rate may be reduced to between 0% and 15% for royalties and 0% and 10% for qualifying interest, subject to beneficial ownership, real economic substance of the recipient, and completion of ETA relief procedures.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Per Egyptian Ministerial Decree No. 110/2018, contemporaneous Transfer Pricing documentation (Local File) is mandatory when the aggregate annual value of controlled transactions between the Egyptian LLC and related parties exceeds EGP 6,000,000. The Master File may also be required for large multinational groups or upon ETA request; Country-by-Country Reporting is required for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of at least EGP 3,500,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not administer a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) filing regime comparable to certain Gulf jurisdictions. Nevertheless, Law No. 91/2005 contains general anti-abuse rules, and the ETA and Egyptian courts will disregard artificial or sham arrangements lacking real economic substance. An affiliate media-buying LLC must have genuine local management, operational staff, physical office or identifiable place of management, commercial contracts, books, bank accounts, and decision-making in Egypt. Without substance, treaty benefits, DTA relief, deduction claims, and the separate legal personality of the LLC may be challenged.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating affiliate commissions, creating fictitious media-ad invoices, inflating traffic-acquisition expenses, or colluding with shell vendors to reduce taxable income and evade 22.5% corporate tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egypt's Income Tax Law No. 91/2005 and the Egyptian Penal Code, tax evasion triggers recovery of the evaded tax, the 2% monthly delay surcharge, monetary fines, and imprisonment. Penalties typically range from fines of EGP 5,000 to EGP 100,000 plus up to five years' imprisonment for fraudulent statements, with the ETA also empowered to seize bank accounts and assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false tax returns or knowingly direct fraudulent transactions are jointly and severally liable. Corporate veil piercing is available where the LLC is used as an instrument of fraud; directors risk personal asset attachment, travel bans, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Egyptian LLC as a letterbox entity with no genuine management, employees, premises, or economic decision-making, while routing profits to a foreign parent; using nominee directors or undisclosed beneficial owners to evade transparency obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA and commercial registry may deny treaty benefits, recharacterize the arrangement, disallow deductions, and impose CIT at the full 22.5% on a gross-revenue or deemed-profit basis. Administrative dissolution of the LLC and revocation of the commercial registration are possible, with fines under Egyptian company and tax law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors are exposed to personal recovery of unpaid taxes and fines where the corporate form is a façade. Travel bans and asset freezes are routinely used in Egyptian tax enforcement against directors; criminal liability for aiding tax evasion can result in imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering in Media-Buying Fund Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using unverified affiliate partners, paying publishing suppliers in cash, cryptocurrency, or layered third-party accounts, or deliberately obscuring the source of performance-media revenue; failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports with Egypt's Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egyptian Law No. 80/2016 (Anti-Money Laundering), penalties include imprisonment of up to 7 years, monetary fines up to EGP 1,000,000, freezing/seizure of funds, and confiscation of the proceeds and instrumentalities of the unlawful transaction. The Financial Regulatory Authority may also revoke permits and impose administrative debarment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners are personally liable for willful failure to comply with KYC and suspicious-transaction reporting duties. Conviction carries imprisonment, permanent travel bans, debarment from board service, and personal confiscation of assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure / Impermissible Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare mandatory Local File/Master File within the EGP 6,000,000 threshold, applying non-arm's-length margins to affiliate media-buying transactions, or distributing dividends without withholding and remitting the 10% WHT and applicable treaty documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA may make a transfer-pricing adjustment, disallow intra-group deductions, recharacterize loans/royalties, and impose additional CIT of 22.5% plus the 2% monthly delay surcharge and fixed administrative fines. Withholding tax that should have been withheld is collected from the Egyptian LLC as agent, with statutory penalties for late remittance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly fail to withhold or remit statutory WHT are personally liable for the unremitted tax. Deliberate TP documentation destruction or false benchmarking exposes directors to criminal tax evasion liability, travel bans, and imprisonment; a director's personal assets may be attached to satisfy the LLC's tax debt where the corporate veil is pierced.
